headline: Diphtheria Prevention in Chicago: The Health Officer's Problem
source: American Journal of Public Health and the Nations Health (PubMed Central)
blurb: This article by Herman N. Bundesen on preventing diphtheria in Chicago ran in the American Journal of Public Health in May 1934, after it was read at a public health meeting in October 1933.

headline: Measles Outbreak among Vaccinated High School Students -- Illinois
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: From December 9, 1983, to January 13, 1984, Sangamon County had 21 measles cases, including 16 high school students whose school records showed they had been vaccinated.

headline: Epidemiologic Notes and Reports Multiple Measles Outbreaks on College Campuses -- Ohio, Massachusetts, Illinois
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Principia College, a Christian Science college in Illinois with 712 students, had 128 confirmed or probable measles cases between January 15 and March 10, 1985, and three deaths that appeared to be related.

headline: Mumps Outbreaks on University Campuses -- Illinois, Wisconsin, South Dakota
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Ten colleges and universities in Illinois reported 183 mumps cases during the 1986-87 school year.

headline: Epidemiologic Notes and Reports Measles Outbreak -- Chicago, 1989
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: By August 23, 1989, Chicago had reported 1,123 confirmed measles cases and four deaths, and 78% of the cases with information were in children under 5.

headline: Use of Mass Tdap Vaccination to Control an Outbreak of Pertussis in a High School --- Cook County, Illinois, September 2006--January 2007
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: After a 17-year-old high school student was reported with whooping cough on September 6, 2006, Cook County health officials linked 36 cases to the school and held a Tdap booster clinic there.

headline: Public Act 099-0249
blurb: This Illinois law, effective August 3, 2015, requires parents who object to school shots on religious grounds to turn in a Certificate of Religious Exemption that states the religious belief and is signed by a health care provider.

headline: Measles Outbreak Associated with a Migrant Shelter — Chicago, Illinois, February–May 2024
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Chicago health officials confirmed a measles case at a temporary shelter for migrants on March 7, 2024, and 57 cases were later tied to the shelter, most of them in people who were not vaccinated.
